blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
External reporting to boards, investors and regulators is a discipline of calibrated precision. Every claim is potentially actionable. Every unhedged forecast can be used, later, as evidence of over-promising, and every omitted caveat can be read as negligence. The writer works within narrow margins, and every margin matters.

Experienced report writers develop a set of habits. They distinguish, in wording, between certainty, expectation and assumption. They attribute material facts to their sources, and they highlight risks explicitly, in a section the reader cannot miss. They avoid phrases such as "we are confident that" unless the confidence can, if challenged, be defended with specific evidence. Such habits are unfashionable when everything is going well, and invaluable when something is not.

The balance, however, is not to retreat into defensive vagueness. Reports that say nothing in twenty pages insult the reader almost as much as reports that overclaim. The craft is to be genuinely informative, while remaining rigorously honest about where confidence is high, where it is moderate, and where reasonable people could disagree.

items.q: According to the text, why is every unhedged forecast risky?
options: It is difficult for investors to understand
It slows down the drafting process
It duplicates the regulator's own analysis
It can later be used as evidence of over-promising
items.why: "Every unhedged forecast can be used, later, as evidence of over-promising."

items.q: How do experienced writers handle the phrase "we are confident that"?
options: They use it to reassure nervous investors
They avoid it unless the confidence can be defended with evidence
They reserve it for the executive summary
They replace it with softer synonyms only
items.why: "They avoid phrases such as 'we are confident that' unless the confidence can… be defended with specific evidence."

items.q: What is the danger of a report that says nothing in twenty pages?
options: It exposes the company to regulators
It is too short to be credible
It insults the reader almost as much as overclaiming
It omits the required risk section
items.why: "Reports that say nothing in twenty pages insult the reader almost as much as reports that overclaim."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Honesty about uncertainty strengthens a report
Caveats should be highlighted where the reader cannot miss them
Material facts should be attributed to their sources
The safest report is one that commits to as little as possible
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita a 'defensive vagueness' — não dizer nada é tão ruim quanto exagerar.

items.q: The final sentence suggests that good reporting requires the writer to…
options: signal clearly which claims are strong and which are debatable
keep controversial judgements out of the report
present every claim with equal confidence
defer entirely to the regulator's view
items.why: Inferência: ser honesto sobre onde a confiança é alta, moderada ou passível de discordância implica graduar cada afirmação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry revisando o relatório trimestral aos investidores. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me talk you through the three paragraphs I've reworked, because the wording matters more than the numbers here.

The original draft said we "will deliver" fifteen per cent growth next quarter. That's a forward-looking statement with no qualification, and if we miss it, someone quotes it back to us. So I've changed it to: we "expect" growth in the low-to-mid teens, subject to market conditions. Same message, but now it reads as an expectation, not a promise.

The second paragraph attributed the demand recovery to "strong fundamentals". That's an opinion dressed up as a fact, so I've attributed it properly — the figure comes from the third-party index, and I've named the source. If a regulator asks where that claim came from, we can point to it.

The third change is the risk section. It was buried on page nineteen, which protects no one. A caveat nobody reads is not a caveat. I've moved it forward and flagged the two factors that could actually move the numbers.

None of this makes the report weaker. It makes it defensible. When things are going well, precise wording feels overcautious. The quarter it stops going well, it's the only thing standing between us and a very awkward conversation.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Harry change "will deliver fifteen per cent" to "expect growth in the low-to-mid teens"?
options: The board requested a lower target
An unqualified promise could be quoted back if missed
The original figure was inaccurate
Investors prefer vaguer numbers
items.why: "That's a forward-looking statement with no qualification, and if we miss it, someone quotes it back to us."

items.q: What was wrong with attributing the recovery to "strong fundamentals"?
options: It was an opinion presented as a fact
It was too technical for investors
It contradicted the third-party index
It repeated the previous quarter's wording
items.why: "That's an opinion dressed up as a fact, so I've attributed it properly."

items.q: What did Harry do with the risk section?
options: Merged it into the growth forecast
Deleted the two minor factors
Left it on page nineteen but shortened it
Moved it forward and flagged the two key factors
items.why: "I've moved it forward and flagged the two factors that could actually move the numbers."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "A caveat nobody reads is not a caveat"?
options: Caveats should be removed to keep reports short
A warning buried out of sight offers no real protection
Only regulators read caveats
Caveats belong exclusively in the appendix
items.why: Inferência: uma ressalva escondida na página 19 não protege ninguém — precisa ser visível para ter valor.

items.q: What is Harry's underlying attitude toward precise wording?
options: It weakens the report's impact on investors
It is a formality that slows reports down
It matters only when regulators are involved
It feels excessive in good times but proves essential in bad ones
items.why: Inferência: "When things are going well, precise wording feels overcautious… the quarter it stops going well, it's the only thing standing between us and a very awkward conversation."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The prospectus contains a full disclosure of related-party transactions." A disclosure is…
options: a confidential internal note
a legal disclaimer that limits liability
the formal act of making information public
a marketing claim
items.why: Disclosure = divulgação, o ato de tornar a informação pública.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Any projection about next year's earnings is a ___ and must carry an explicit qualification."
options: material fact
forward-looking statement
risk factor
disclosure
items.why: Forward-looking statement = declaração prospectiva, uma projeção sobre o futuro.

items.q: "We added the figure only after we could attribute it to the auditor's report." To attribute means to…
options: challenge its accuracy
estimate an approximate value
trace something back to its source and credit it there
remove it from the public version
items.why: To attribute = atribuir, indicar de onde vem a informação.

items.q: A caveat in a report is…
options: a legally binding guarantee
a qualification or warning that limits how a claim should be read
a summary of key results
an appendix of raw data
items.why: Caveat = ressalva, condição que limita a leitura de uma afirmação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The board asked us to list every ___ that could threaten the forecast, from FX volatility to supply disruption."
options: disclosure
qualification
caveat
risk factor
items.why: Risk factor = fator de risco, aquilo que pode ameaçar a previsão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem ao preparar relatórios para conselhos e investidores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the wording before we publish." To sign off on means to…
options: reword entirely
circulate for comment
postpone indefinitely
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the growth figure, calling it too aggressive." They…
options: resisted or challenged it
rewrote the whole report
approved it without comment
asked for it to be published sooner
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let me walk you through the three changes I've made." To walk someone through something is to…
options: defend it against criticism
guide them step by step
hand them the document to read alone
summarise it in one line
items.why: Walk someone through = conduzir alguém passo a passo pelo conteúdo.

items.q: "The forecast is subject to market conditions." This phrase signals that the outcome…
options: has already been achieved
is guaranteed regardless of the market
was approved by the regulator
depends on and may be limited by external conditions
items.why: Subject to = sujeito a; condiciona o resultado a fatores externos — a marca da redação calibrada.

items.q: "Softening every claim won't move the needle on the regulator's concerns." This means it will…
options: attract legal scrutiny
create unnecessary delay
reassure the investors
make no noticeable difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
